import.title: Import
import.textPlaceholder:

die Lampe — lamp
import.noBooks: No processed books yet. Upload one on the Books page.
import.ankiHelp: AnkiWeb has no import link, so export your deck from Anki (File → Export → Anki Deck Package) and upload the .apkg here. Study progress is preserved; cloze notes become grammar cards and reversed notes become two-sided vocab.

import.ankiTruncated: Note: only the first {{max}} notes were imported (the rest were skipped to stay within limits).

study.allDoneHint: No more cards due in this deck. Come back later — or add more.

stats.title: Performance
stats.subtitle: How your reviews are going, and what's coming next.
stats.retentionSub: of {{count}} reviews on cards you'd already learned, last {{range}}. Above 85% means the intervals are about right.
stats.retentionNone: No reviews on learned cards yet — this fills in once cards graduate.
stats.reviewsPerDayHint: Split by how far along each card was when you answered it.
stats.gradesHint: A healthy mix leans on Good. Lots of Again means cards need reworking.
stats.bestHourHint: When you review, and how well it goes. Hover for retention at that hour.
stats.forecastHint: The next 30 days. Anything already overdue is counted today.
stats.compositionHint: Mature cards have an interval of 21 days or more — they're the ones that have stuck.
stats.intervalsHint: How far out your learned cards are scheduled. The weight should drift right over time.
stats.consistencyHint: Showing up beats cramming — the streak is the metric that predicts the rest.
stats.perDeckHint: Counts are each deck's own cards; retention covers the selected range.
stats.toughestHint: The cards you forget most. Rewriting one is usually faster than out-grinding it.
stats.lapsesTitle: Times this card went from learned back to relearning
stats.noLeeches: Nothing is fighting back yet — no card has lapsed.
stats.blankHint: Study a deck and this page fills in: retention, streaks, what's coming due, and which cards are giving you trouble.

practice.sub_write: Write a passage, get it corrected, and turn each mistake into a card.
practice.sub_speak: Hold a conversation out loud — it replies, and flags what to fix.
practice.sub_read: Read a passage aloud and see which words came through.
practice.referenceEmpty: Get a text to translate, or just start writing below — both get corrected.
practice.readEmpty: Get a passage, then read it aloud.
practice.typeHint: Type a message in {{lang}} to get started.

welcome.nameLede: A first name is plenty — it's only used to say hello.
welcome.decksLede: A card is one thing you're learning — a word, a phrase, a grammar rule. A deck is a folder of cards, and decks can sit inside other decks.
welcome.decksNote: Vocabulary is studied both ways — shown the word, and shown the meaning.
welcome.reviewTitle: You only review what you're about to forget
welcome.reviewLede: I show you a card, you try to answer, then you tell me how it went:
welcome.reviewNote: Again brings it back soon. Easy makes it wait longer. That's spaced repetition — it keeps the daily work small and the memory fresh.
welcome.featImportBody: Paste a word list or bring an Anki deck — the cards get built for you.
welcome.featBooksBody: Upload a coursebook PDF and pull the vocabulary out of each lesson.
welcome.featPracticeBody: Write, speak out loud, or read a passage — and get corrected.
welcome.featStatsBody: Streaks, how much is sticking, and what's coming due.
